name: SHELF DOMINION: Territory & Debt
description: A brutal territory-control board game played on a modular hexagonal map of the Gray Zone, where players represent rival gang factions, corponation proxies, and mutual aid networks competing for district control through debt mechanics and resource scarcity. Smart-ink tiles shift faction colors in real time as control changes hands, the board physically darkening in contested zones. Originally printed on salvaged packaging material by a Tier 1 collective in Milwaukee-Under, the game spread through the Gray Zone bars within two years of its first run.
story_hooks: A player discovers the game's original designer embedded a hidden faction — the Cartographers — whose win condition involves mapping every district's debt network and broadcasting it publicly, triggering a real-world hunt for the master copy.
A the Gray Zone bar's weekly SHELF DOMINION tournament becomes the de facto negotiation table for three rival gangs, and a PC is asked to throw a game to prevent a turf war from going hot.
Someone is printing a new edition with subtly altered debt mechanics that benefit one real faction over others — and the change is so technically embedded that only a game theory expert would notice.
